A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-decomposition method. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-response simulations, comparisons of information measures, and diffusion-based MNIST attribution results, including supplementary examples and an additivity experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds natural-image attribution using a fitted retinal-response model and an MNIST receptive-field perturbation experiment.

M1.justification: The Ilocal definition, feature-wise decomposition, conditional and unconditional diffusion models, and approximate Monte Carlo estimation procedure remain unchanged. The revised neural encoders serve as experimental settings for the same attribution method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.6 extends coverage from synthetic examples and MNIST to Tiny ImageNet natural images and a neural encoder fitted to retinal ganglion-cell recordings. This substantially broadens the represented stimuli and neural population. Gaussian-prior comparisons and additional MNIST digits already existed in v1.

E2.justification: The MNIST comparisons expand beyond Fisher information to include Isurp against Ilocal in the new receptive-field perturbation experiment, Figure 8. Isurp was already evaluated in v1's one-dimensional experiments; the existing comparator sets elsewhere are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 revises the reported MNIST encoder: RF width changes from 0.2 to 0.1, gain from 1.0 to 0.4, threshold from 0.5 to 0.9, and the firing-rate formula gains a scale of 40 with a changed sigmoid expression. C.6–C.7 add retinal-model and RF-perturbation protocols. These are substantive reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained MNIST results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.7 and Figure 8 add a focused locality analysis: perturb neuron 21's receptive field with a distant Gaussian bump and compare changes in Ilocal and Isurp. The earlier prior-sensitivity, one-dimensional locality, data-processing, and additivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: The disclosed Monte Carlo sampling remains 50 noisy samples per evaluated diffusion step. v2 introduces no repeated-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds information maps for three natural images, reporting concentration around high-contrast object boundaries. Figure 8 adds perturbation difference maps showing more spatially confined changes for Ilocal than Isurp. These substantially extend the qualitative results. The original MNIST images in Figures 4 and 6 are identical across versions, rather than evidence of improved performance.

T1.justification: Axiom 2 gains explicit tolerance-and-distance quantifiers and an infinite-support condition. Section 4.1 adds finite-moment assumptions and a positive-noise cutoff followed by monotone convergence. Appendix A replaces the earlier approximate locality argument with separate finite-noise and tail derivations presenting exponential decay and a uniform inverse-cutoff bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: an axiomatic local information decomposition, feature-wise attribution, and scalable diffusion-based estimation. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly explains that locality conflicts with invariance to invertible stimulus-coordinate transformations. The revised theoretical passages also make domain and finite-moment restrictions explicit. The existing limitation concerning unproven uniqueness remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Alongside revised MNIST encoder specifications, C.6 documents 60,000 natural training images at 64×64 resolution, fitting responses from 41 retinal cells, and constructing a 49-field mosaic from one fitted cell. The code link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository and lists the additional figures. Existing diffusion training and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Goldin et al. (2022) and Klindt et al. (2017) for the retinal application and removes the Rioul (2010) citation. It adds a positioning argument about coordinate invariance versus locality, while retaining the principal comparisons with Fisher information and Kong et al.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most introductory and discussion prose remain stable. Local revisions expand theoretical explanations, clarify experiments, divide Appendix A into two subproofs, and add appendix subsections and acknowledgements. Author affiliations are also expanded.

P2.justification: The visual evidence is substantially expanded: Figure 1 gains a Fisher-information panel, Figure 2 adds Gaussian-prior/posterior panels, and new Figures 7–8 display natural-image and perturbation results. Existing figures are resized or relocated, and the author block is extensively reformatted. Table 1 and the original MNIST image panels remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's synthetic and MNIST demonstrations, C.6–C.7 provide useful additional support through natural images, a fitted retinal model, and a targeted perturbation test. Explicit theoretical assumptions also improve transparency. The gains remain limited: the new empirical evidence is qualitative, and substantial encoder-setting revisions are unexplained while the original MNIST result images are retained.
